# FlashAlpha sample-chain fixture

Original bytes from [FlashAlpha-lab/gex-explained](https://github.com/FlashAlpha-lab/gex-explained/tree/a11321d62006311c4a72a68552587485024f2bf2), retrieved 2026-09-26. Upstream commit: a11321d62006311c4a72a68552587485024f2bf2. This is the original upstream demonstration sample, not a replacement generated by FLOWW and not a verified historical market capture.

- [sample_chain.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlashAlpha-lab/gex-explained/a11321d62006311c4a72a68552587485024f2bf2/data/sample_chain.csv): SHA256 6e1e6617916580ae60ff9d5e6327f16e1da36992744fa8e29ba98364918d4b54; 25 contracts, 13 strikes, sample spot590, expiry2026-03-21.
- [MIT licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlashAlpha-lab/gex-explained/a11321d62006311c4a72a68552587485024f2bf2/LICENSE): SHA256 f74471056c5088727be5fb5a638db72f1f9612134d4a09e91718fe3b2b536e1c; copyright2026 FlashAlpha Lab. The complete notice is retained beside the sample.

The tests use an explicitly modeled valuation date2026-02-19 (30calendar days before the sample expiry). That date is a fixed test assumption, not claimed source-observation provenance. The pre-existing moneyness-based volatility assumption is also test-only, not observed/implied market volatility or proof of executable prices. Freezing this date removes dependence on the day the test runs. No production data/calculation path is changed.

The restored sample also exactly matches the already-committed qc/data/flashalpha_sample_chain_manifest.json (ingested2026-05-18,25rows,1172bytes,sameSHA256). That historical manifest is preserved unchanged. Git attributes retain the original CSV/licence bytes on Windows, and the fixture loader verifies the CSV digest before testing.
